recipes.name: Sausage Balls
ingredients_raw: 1 pound ground pork sausage, at room temperature

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Combine sausage and biscuit mix in a large bowl; mix with your hands until evenly combined. Add Cheddar and continue mixing until the mixture holds together. It may seem dry at first, but there’s no need to add liquid.
Shape the mixture into about 30 balls, each about 1 ½ inches wide, and arrange them on a rimmed baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the centers registers 160 degrees F (71 degrees C), 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sausage Balls
raw_recipe.description: Make these 3-ingredient sausage balls with pork sausage, biscuit mix, and sharp Cheddar for an easy, crowd-pleasing breakfast or holiday appetizer.

video.description: In this video, join us in the kitchen for a delightful culinary adventure as we show you how to make mouthwatering Sausage Balls. This easy-to-follow recipe will guide you through the steps of combining sausage, cheddar cheese, and baking mix to create perfect bite-sized snacks. Whether you're hosting a party, planning a brunch, or just craving a savory treat, these Sausage Balls are the ideal choice. Whip up a batch and savor the savory goodness!

review.reviewBody: These are really good. I have a few pointers. Too make ingred. mix better together-- mix sausage with Biscuit THEN add cheese. The ball don't have the powdery white appearance and they mix easier. Also I like to cook these on parchment paper and they slide right off the paper. Enjoy.

I learned how to make sausage cheese balls in high school and have used the same recipe for over 10 years. My family has requested these at every baby and bridal shower until I have gotten sick of making them and even eating them. The only difference in the way I make them and this is that I cook them longer. They really need to cook for up to 25 minutes. Otherwise you end up with raw sausage in the middle. I have tried different brands of sausage and it makes a difference. Some are greasier than others and some are drier. And I have found that Aberdeen sausage (spelling?) (it may be Aberdeen Farms) works the best. You can find it at walmart and it usually is the cheapest. If the ones on the edge of your pan end up dry just put all the sausage balls in a covered container and let them sit covered until they cool. The steam will help the dry ones become moist. I always cover mine to cool to hold in the flavor even if they don't dry out because it seems to make them taste even better if the flavors mingle.
I tried this recipe but with one change..use stove top stuffing instead of baking mix..it adds so much flavor!!!!

This is the recipe I've used for 20+ years, adding another good handful more of cheddar. I can't believe some recommend to cook the sausage before mixing. No, you do NOT cook the sausage first! Your sausage balls will be dry and lacking the flavor the grease gives them during baking. Just toss them in a paper-towel lined bowl to absorb any excess grease afterward. If you use nice sausage (it really is worth a buck or two more), you won't have the super greasy problem to begin with. If you live in the southeast, look for Neese's Hot Sausage (the BEST!). Failing that, Jimmy Dean is fine (don't go lower in quality than that, tho). Set the ingredients out an hour ahead of time. You have to use some muscle to get it totally blended. You'll know it's ready when you can smoosh it into one big old smooth mass that isn't crumbly or dry. DON'T add liquid if it seems dry - that isn't the problem! The warmth of your hands and the kneading will do the trick. Just keep at it; it'll end up just right. I make mine large-marble size (ends up walnut size after baking) and cook about 15 mins. This is THE recipe to try. Don't use tons of baking mix or add liquids like some recipes call for. Use parchment/silpat; the bottoms won't over-brown or stick. For heaven's sake - whatever you do - DO NOT precook the sausage! :)

I've made these several times. In fact, we have been told not to bring them to Thanksgiving on account that they were too popular and the hostess didn't like that they stole the show. So...we don't go to their house for thanksgiving any longer and do our own thing. For all the people that say these were dry and cakey. KEEP MIXING. You're looking for a chunky pink playdough type look only not as smooth. I tend to add 2 TBL of water while mixing to help things come together. Hot Breakfast sausage is a must. Fresh grated Extra sharp Tillamook Cheddar cheese makes a huge difference. We've even made it with Gluten free Bisquick before. With gluten free mix you can mix it forever and it wont get tough to handle. I use a small cookie scoop so I don't have to handle them so much and scrape up the sides of the bowl. Then just squeeze them out flat side down on a piece of nonstick foil.

I've been making these for years and they are a family favorite. I use Jimmy Dean Hot sausage. My mom's recipe also states to add a 1/4 cup of water (or more) as needed to make slightly moist balls. Ours turn out perfectly. I usually double the batch and take to family gatherings. Using the sausage at room temperature works best and I cut everything together with 2 forks rather than a food processor. I use lightweight, clear vinyl gloves to roll the balls and parchment paper instead of greasing the pan. Hope this helps.

Made these as directed. Used half regular sausage and half spicy. Bob Evans brand. Notes: Sausage MUST be room temp in order for biscuit mix to mix in properly. I mixed a little at a time, working it in thoroughly each time I added more. It's a forearms workout. DO NOT use pre-shredded cheese. I also mixed in the cheese bit by bit. Photo shows what it looked like after it was all mixed together. I used a cookie scoop to make the sausage balls the same size, but still had to roll them in my palms to press together well. Family LOVED them! Served with a dip made of two parts mayo to one part spicy brown mustard and a pinch of garlic powder.

Being a born & raised Southerner, I’ve been eating - and making - these morsels my entire life. My Mawmaw made a change (& swore me to secrecy!) to include about an 1/8 cup Campbell’s Cheddar Cheese Soup, with a tad of water, added a bit at a time while adding the cheese. I’ve never had dry sausage balls since! Enjoy!!

I have made these for years for family meals. People look forward to them. Last year, I was feeling frisky and substituted Red Lobster Cheddar Bay biscuit mix for the Bisquick. They were amazing! I will make them that way from now on.

This is one of our favorite Christmas treats. I used my kitchen aide mixer to mix everything together. Then I put it in the refrigerator until it is chilled - I think it is easier to roll the sausage into balls. Cabot seriously sharp cheese and Jimmy Dean HOT sausage is the way to go in this recipe.
Very good but alittle dry. But 2nd time I made them I added 8oz of cream cheese and used hot sausage. very moist
These are a great snack. Perfect for potluck. The sausage balls come together very easy and the recipes makes a lot, definately a crowd pleaser.
Family loves these. Not the healthiest for gastric sleeve surg.
So tasty! Definitely recommend using this recipe!!
I had made these years ago and had forgotten about them, until seeing them on here. I just made them today for a function at church and definitely a crowd pleaser!
Very easy to make. Delightfully tasty!!!
It was ok. Not very flavorful.
I used the Red Lobster cheddar biscuit mix rather than bisquic.
This is my go to recipe for quick breakfast balls...I <3 it! Thanks for the tip to mix baking mix and sausage first, then the cheese...it is so much easier....:)..
It was easy and delicious
